clue.text: Unfinished area of church is a hazard

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: A half-built part of a church poses a danger to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the last letter, L, from CHANCEL; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance can mean a risk or hazard, as in 'take a chance'.

clue.text: Don't be ridiculous — get down from there

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief at nonsense

explanation.surface: Telling someone to stop being silly and climb down.
explanation.definitionFit: Come off it is a scornful retort, and literally means dismount from something.

clue.text: Hebridean island's execution, a hanging

indicators.note: execution suggests beheading, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Barra is an island of the Outer Hebrides, in western Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish island's public hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' beheads BARRA'S, removing B. 'Hanging' is not death by rope but a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry hung on a wall, named after the French town famous for weaving it.

clue.text: Cows unknown to take a showy orchid

parts.note: cows are cattle
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Grazing cattle sample a flamboyant flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattleya is a genus of tropical orchids with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Stay at home during the holidays

definitions.text: Stay at home during the holidays

parts.words: Stay at home during the holidays
parts.note: reads like staying in your own home over the break, but means looking after someone else's home while they are away

explanation.surface: Someone skips going away and stays put over the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: To housesit is to live in and mind another person's house while the owners are on holiday.

clue.text: Having no problems sleeping away from home — not want to be in dark?

definitions.text: away from home — not want to be in dark?
definitions.meaning: out means not at home, and a light that is out would rather not be, so it is in the dark

explanation.surface: A traveller who sleeps well yet fears the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out like a light is to fall asleep very quickly, and the phrase also describes a lamp switched off.

clue.text: One charring for a musician

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady moonlights as a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charring' tempts as doing housework, a charwoman's job; here it means burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer is one who sings, and also one who singes or chars something.

clue.text: Slam rebel organisation that counts for little

indicators.note: organising letters means arranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel group calling for a slam is insignificant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges SLAM and REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for something trivial or unimportant.

clue.text: Daughter in big loss over house

indicators.note: the daughter's letter goes in the middle of the turned word
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A daughter suffers heavy losses on a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROUT to TUOR, and D goes inside. 'house' is a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Roman poet I put forward for marriage

indicators.note: an item put forward is moved nearer the front, so one letter shifts to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: Martial was a Latin poet famous for his epigrams

explanation.surface: A classical poet proposes marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I put forward' moves the I in MARTIAL one place earlier, before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective describing anything relating to marriage, matching the adjectival 'for marriage'.

clue.text: Blameless' rise, after a fashion, is novel

indicators.note: in some fashion means in a different manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blameless person's rise somehow makes something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the adjective meaning new; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Misérables is the novel by Victor Hugo.

clue.text: Giving thanks, drank off this?

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grateful drinker downs a toast from a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, then NKARD, an anagram of DRANK signalled by 'off'. The whole clue also describes the answer: what you drink from when giving thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, the vessel you might drain while toasting.

clue.text: Ring bird by lake, following old custom

indicators.note: following places the lake abbreviation after the custom

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
use in the old sense means custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: A bird encircles a lake as tradition dictates.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a thrush-family bird such as the blackbird or ring ousel.

clue.text: One twisting chair found in' Curiosity Shop

definitions.meaning: a person or seat that swivels round
Dick ... is a character in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A revolving seat turns up in an antiques store.
explanation.definitionFit: A swiveller is literally one that swivels, and Dick Swiveller is the Dickens clerk in that novel.

clue.text: Seeker after gold has to square monarch

parts.note: forty-nine is a square number, seven times seven
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A prospector has to settle accounts with the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is a noun here, a square number; 'has to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-niners were the prospectors who rushed to California in 1849 seeking gold.

clue.text: Shape of playground a confused matter

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British word for a playground or park
a tangle is a confused muddle

explanation.surface: Describing a messy playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. A rec is the local recreation ground in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided shape with right angles.

clue.text: Less than half the' Frenchmen in dining-room

indicators.note: keeping less than half of a word means only its opening few letters survive, four of nine here

parts.note: messieurs is French for gentlemen, plural of monsieur

explanation.surface: Only a few of the Frenchmen are in the dining-room.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep MESS, four of the nine letters of MESSIEURS; 'the' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a dining-room for military personnel, as in the officers' mess.

clue.text: Being so deters' any movement

indicators.note: movement among letters shifts them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Being inactive puts you off moving at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges DETERS and ANY. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: being inactive prevents movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary means sitting a lot and inactive, which discourages movement.

clue.text: Nervous about tirade, but showing assurance

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the other

parts.note: wary means cautious or nervous
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A nervous person's rant still conveys confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the nervous word round the tirade; 'but showing' is a link, and 'assurance' means a guarantee rather than confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee, an assurance that goods will work.

clue.text: Nail down direction of policy

definitions.meaning: to fasten with small nails, as a carpet is fixed
a course of action, as in 'try a different approach'

explanation.surface: Settling the course a policy will take.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack is to fix with tacks, and a tack is also a course or line of approach, from sailing.

clue.text: Players in America' very angry with endless journey

parts.note: real is American slang for very, as in 'real good'
mad means angry

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Sports players in the US get furious after a long trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is a Spanish football club, so a team of players.

clue.text: No longer resting as actor? .Not entirely

definitions.meaning: resting is theatre slang for out of work, so an actor who has work is in a role

explanation.surface: A performer is only partly back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: In part means partly, and read literally it describes an actor cast in a role.

clue.text: Working group 'of well-connected criminals

parts.note: suggests a gang with good contacts, but means convicts literally chained together while labouring

explanation.surface: A team of criminals with influential contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of prisoners chained together for outdoor labour.

clue.text: Trophy I would give boy with little bow

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone would award a cup to a boy with a small bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of love, a winged boy carrying a small bow and arrows.

clue.text: Flee, punching me in stomach

indicators.note: a word punching another breaks into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to flee is to run

explanation.surface: Someone escaping lands a blow in my belly.
explanation.walkthrough: ME goes into RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumen is the first stomach of a cud-chewing animal such as a cow.

clue.text: One going to work in building, 'since start of week's. come round

definitions.text: One going to work in building

indicators.note: to come round something is to encircle it, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday, the start of the week
as means since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'

explanation.surface: A worker goes in because the week has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come round' wraps the weekday abbreviation round the word for since; the definition hints at a stonemason, not a builder heading to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason works in building, laying stone or brick.

clue.text: Queue has unpleasant person at back'

parts.note: a pig is a greedy or nasty person
the tail is the back end of something

explanation.surface: A line of people has a horrible person at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queue' is an old word for a plait of hair, not a line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue in the old sense is a pigtail, a plait hanging at the back of the head.

clue.text: In this country, is one surrounded by fish?

indicators.note: something surrounded by another sits inside it, so these letters go within the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone in this land is ringed by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts the two short pieces inside the fish. The held text was an OCR garble; the scan prints 'is one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country on the Mediterranean, a sea known for tuna.

clue.text: Player with partner' is breaking several times: now expected to go' first

indicators.note: to go first puts this piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: due means expected, as in 'the train is due'

indicators.note: breaking into a group means getting inside it

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time, so three Ts are several times

explanation.surface: A partnered musician breaks off often but is now due on first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is breaking' puts IS among three Ts, giving TTIST; 'to go first' fronts the word for expected, and 'now' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A duettist performs a duet, playing or singing with one partner.

clue.text: With heartless stupidity, disdain every Olympic venue

indicators.note: heartless words lose their insides, leaving only the first and last letters of each

explanation.surface: Someone scorns a games host city with stupid contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps the first and last letters of each of the three words: SY, DN, EY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2000.
